\section{Declarations}

\begin{lemma}[Log-space bound by the input parameter]
\lean{Complexity.logSpace_le_succ}
\label{Complexity.logSpace_le_succ}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.logSpace}
\difficulty{3}
For every $n\in\mathbb{N}$, if $\ell(n)=\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor+1$ for positive $n$ and
$\ell(0)=1$, then $\ell(n)\le n+1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Logarithmic space is contained in polynomial space]
\lean{Complexity.LOGSPACE_subset_PSPACE}
\label{Complexity.LOGSPACE_subset_PSPACE}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LOGSPACE, Complexity.PSPACE, Complexity.SPACE.mono, Complexity.logSpace_le_succ, Complexity.space_poly_subset_PSPACE}
\difficulty{1}
Every binary language decidable by a finite Turing machine using at most $c(\log_2 n+1)$
work-tape cells on inputs of length $n$, for some natural number $c$, belongs to the
class of languages decidable using at most $c'(n^{c'}+1)$ work-tape cells for some
natural number $c'.$
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Polynomial space contains shifted power space]
\lean{Complexity.SPACE_succ_pow_subset_PSPACE}
\label{Complexity.SPACE_succ_pow_subset_PSPACE}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.PSPACE, Complexity.SPACE, Complexity.SPACE.mono_const, Complexity.space_poly_subset_PSPACE, Complexity.succ_pow_le}
\difficulty{1}
For every natural number $k$, the class of binary languages decidable with space bounded
by a constant multiple of $(n+1)^k$ is contained in the class of languages decidable in
polynomial space.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Log-space bound from an exponential bound]
\lean{Complexity.logSpace_le_of_le_mul_two_pow}
\label{Complexity.logSpace_le_of_le_mul_two_pow}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.logSpace}
\difficulty{4}
Define $\ell(v)=\lfloor\log_2 v\rfloor+1$ for positive integers $v$, and set
$\ell(0)=1$. If $v\le A2^s$ and $1\le s$, then $\ell(v)\le(A+1)s$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Space simulation by an arithmetic register program]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.arm_decides_space}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.arm_decides_space}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.AHalt, Complexity.LogProg.ARM, Complexity.LogProg.Pre, Complexity.LogProg.PreS, Complexity.LogProg.armProg, Complexity.LogProg.arm_space, Complexity.LogProg.arun, Complexity.LogProg.bankK, Complexity.LogProg.bankStart, Complexity.LogProg.bankTM, Complexity.LogProg.bank_cleanRun, Complexity.LogProg.cleanRun_mono, Complexity.LogProg.compileFinTM, Complexity.LogProg.length_bits_mono, Complexity.LogProg.length_callSegs_le, Complexity.SPACE, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.DecidesInSpace, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator}
\difficulty{7}
Let $L$ be a language of Boolean strings, let $A$ be an arithmetic register program with
a finite state set, and choose an initial state $l_0$. For each of the finitely many
oracle languages $A_j$, let $s_j$ be a space bound, and suppose each $A_j$ is decidable
in space $s_j$. Let $S,W:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ and $C\in\mathbb{N}$ satisfy $1\le
S(n)$ and $W(n)\le C S(n)$ for every $n$, and suppose $s_j(v)\le C S(n)$ whenever $v\le
2n+2+m(2W(n)+2)$. If, on every input $x$, the program started in state $l_0$ with all
registers zero halts with the answer deciding membership in $L$, and throughout the run
every register has a canonical binary representation of length at most $W(|x|)$ while
the stated step preconditions hold, then $L$ is decidable in space $O(S(n))$
(equivalently, $L\in\mathrm{SPACE}(S)$).
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Oracle register programs in space S]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.arm_decides_SPACE}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.arm_decides_SPACE}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LOGSPACE, Complexity.LogProg.AHalt, Complexity.LogProg.ARM, Complexity.LogProg.PreS, Complexity.LogProg.arm_decides_space, Complexity.LogProg.succ_le_two_pow_log, Complexity.SPACE, Complexity.logSpace, Complexity.logSpace_le_of_le_mul_two_pow, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.DecidesInSpace, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator}
\difficulty{6}
Let $L$ be a language of bit strings, let $A$ be a register program with $m$ registers
and finitely many states, and let $\ell_0$ be its initial state. Suppose there are $d$
oracle languages $A_0,\ldots,A_{d-1}$, each decidable in logarithmic space, and
functions $S:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ and a natural number $K$ such that $\lfloor\log_2
n\rfloor+1\le S(n)$ for every $n$. Suppose also that, on each input $x$, the run from
$\ell_0$ with all registers zero halts with the correct membership answer for $L$, and
every configuration before halting satisfies the program's side conditions and has, for
every register $r$, binary length of $r$'s value plus one at most $K S(|x|)$. Then $L$
belongs to the space class $\mathrm{SPACE}(S)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Polynomial-space oracle register computations]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.arm_decides_pspace}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.arm_decides_pspace}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.AHalt, Complexity.LogProg.ARM, Complexity.LogProg.PreS, Complexity.LogProg.arm_decides_space, Complexity.PSPACE, Complexity.SPACE_succ_pow_subset_PSPACE, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.DecidesInSpace, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator}
\difficulty{6}
Let $L$ be a language of bit strings, let $A$ be a register program with $m$ registers
and finitely many states, and let $\ell_0$ be its initial state. Suppose there are $d$
oracle languages $A_0,\ldots,A_{d-1}$, each decidable in polynomial space, and natural
numbers $C_0,c_0$. If, on every input $x$, the run from $\ell_0$ with all registers zero
halts with the correct membership answer for $L$, and every configuration before halting
satisfies the program's side conditions and has each register's binary length after
adding one at most $C_0(|x|+1)^{c_0}$, then $L$ is decidable in polynomial space.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Exponential register values and polynomial space]
